steps.title: Fayol and beyond
steps.body:
Classical management theory (Henri Fayol, early 1900s) describes managerial work as planning, organising, commanding and controlling. Modern texts use **planning, organising, leading, controlling (POLC)**.

Mintzberg observed that real managers also play interpersonal, informational and decisional roles, mostly in short, interrupted tasks.

steps.title: Example
steps.body:
- Setting next quarter's output target = **planning**
- Reassigning two supervisors to night shift = **organising**
- Motivating a stressed team before a deadline = **leading**
- Comparing defect rate with the 2% standard = **controlling**

steps.body:
- Thinking management is only control.
- Treating the functions as a strict sequence; in practice they overlap and loop.

steps.title: Core theories
steps.body: **Maslow:** needs hierarchy (physiological, safety, belonging, esteem, self-actualisation). **Herzberg:** hygiene factors (pay, conditions) prevent dissatisfaction; motivators (achievement, recognition, growth) create satisfaction. **Vroom's expectancy:** motivation = Expectancy × Instrumentality × Valence. **Locke:** specific, challenging goals improve performance.

steps.title: Expectancy example
steps.body: Expectancy 0.8 (effort → performance), instrumentality 0.5 (performance → reward), valence 8. Motivation score = 0.8 × 0.5 × 8 = **3.2**. If any factor is zero, motivation is zero.

steps.title: Common mistake
steps.body: Assuming money motivates everyone equally; Herzberg's pay is a hygiene factor.

lessons.title: Time value of money: why ₹1 today beats ₹1 tomorrow

scenes.text: Aarav is offered ₹1,00,000 today or ₹1,08,000 after one year from a stable borrower. A fixed deposit pays 7%.

steps.title: Core formulas
steps.body:
Future value: **FV = PV × (1+r)^n**. Present value: **PV = FV / (1+r)^n**. Discount rate r reflects opportunity cost and risk.

An ordinary annuity (payments at period end) has **PV = C × [1 − (1+r)^−n] / r**.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: ₹1,00,000 at 7% for 1 year → ₹1,07,000. The ₹1,08,000 offer is better by ₹1,000 in year-1 money, if risk is equal.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body: Mixing a monthly rate with annual periods; using nominal rate for compounding without dividing by m; forgetting annuity-due (start of period) needs ×(1+r).

steps.title: Effective annual rate
steps.body: EAR = (1 + APR/m)^m − 1. A 12% nominal rate compounded monthly has EAR ≈ 12.68%.

steps.title: EMI formula
steps.body: EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n / [(1+r)^n − 1], with r = annual rate/12 and n = months.

steps.title: Set-up
steps.body: r = 0.085/12 = 0.0070833; n = 240. Use the equivalent annuity form EMI = P·r / [1 − (1+r)^−n].

steps.title: Sanity check
steps.body: Total paid = EMI × n. Interest = total − principal. For long loans, interest often exceeds principal.

steps.title: Quick calculations

steps.title: Interpretation
